facts.claim: LoRA freezes a pre-trained model's weights and adds small trainable low-rank matrices to each layer of the Transformer.
Against GPT-3 175B fine-tuned with Adam, LoRA's authors report 10,000 times fewer trainable parameters and a third of the GPU memory.

Biderman and colleagues found that in the standard low-rank settings LoRA learns substantially less than full fine-tuning, but keeps more of the base model's performance outside the target domain: it learns less and forgets less.
Catastrophic forgetting is a neural network losing what it learned before when it is trained on something new; Kirkpatrick and colleagues note it was long thought to be unavoidable.
Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) trains a model on pairs of preferred and rejected answers with a simple classification loss, without a separate reward model or reinforcement learning.
OpenAI's model-optimization guide starts with evals that measure the model's output to set a baseline, and suggests writing them even before the prompts.
OpenAI's model-optimization guide says prompt engineering may be all you need, and presents fine-tuning as an option for some tasks.

OpenAI's guide lists tasks fine-tuning suits, such as classification, a specific output format and fixing instruction-following failures, and training a smaller, cheaper, faster model to excel at one task.

On May 7, 2026, OpenAI told developers its self-serve fine-tuning was winding down: closed that day to organizations that had never fine-tuned, from July 2, 2026 to those with no fine-tuned inference in the past 60 days, and to new training jobs for active customers on January 6, 2027.
OpenAI says inference on fine-tuned models stops only when the underlying base model is deprecated.

Ovadia and colleagues (2023) found that fetching documents (RAG) consistently beat fine-tuning on raw text across their knowledge tests, both for facts the model had seen in training and for brand-new ones.
Zhou and colleagues (2023) fine-tuned a 65-billion-weight LLaMa model on only 1,000 hand-picked prompts and replies, and it learnt to follow the replies’ formats.

Gekhman and colleagues (2024) found that models learn new facts through fine-tuning much more slowly than facts they already know, and that once learnt, those new facts make them more likely to make things up.
